data_quality.verdict: A NULL test is not a resolution test: the columns are NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, so unresolved picks are stored as 0.00%. Plotting 'resolved' as pnl IS NOT NULL therefore counts 21194 flat trades as results, and the raw mean (+21.03%) is carried by 463 picks outside +/-50%. Cleaning it (zeros dropped, |PnL| <= 50%) leaves 41932 picks at a +0.281% mean - but the median is only +0.057% and the 10th/90th percentiles are -14.69%/+17.36%, so that mean is a right tail, not typical performance. At a 0.26% round turn the median pick costs more than it earns.

prediction_set.subject: Estate-wide cost gate, judged on the MEDIAN pick
prediction_set.claim: The typical pick does not pay for its costs: forward median net <= 0 after a 0.26% round turn, even though the mean stays positive.
prediction_set.basis: Cleaned median is +0.057% (5.7bp) against a 26bp round turn; the +0.281% mean is a right tail (p10 -14.69%, p90 +17.36%). EQUITY +3.60%, ETF +0.76%, FOREX +0.47% and FUTURES +0.26% clear 26bp on the MEAN - which is why this prediction is stated on the median: a mean that only survives on its best decile is not a repeatable edge.
prediction_set.kill: I am wrong if the forward median exceeds +0.26% on 1,000 picks.
